test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 1 (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
**Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. The first is far more real than the second.

B. But, a person who enjoys long-distance popularity succeeds in creating a favorable notion of himself among unknown people.

C. An intimately popular person is liked by those who know him.

D. There are two kinds of popularity - intimate and long-distance popularity.
solution:
The correct answer is 'DACB.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "**the kinds of popularity i.e. intimate and long-distance popularity**". Hence, 'D' is the first part.
 
• Sentence A will come after D as it is giving information about the **intimate** popularity which is far more real than long-distance popularity.
 
• Sentence C will come after A as it further describes an intimately popular person who is liked by those who know him.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding part as it explains the second kind of popularity i.e a** ****long-distance popular person** who** ****succeeds in creating f**avorable notion of himself among unknown people.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *There are two kinds of popularity - intimate and long-distance popularity. The first is far more real than the second. An intimately popular person is liked by those who know him. But, a person who enjoys long-distance popularity succeeds in creating a favorable notion of himself among unknown people.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
